findings.claim: The watch's default state file RECEIPT_DIR/basis_watch_state.json is written into the shared receipt directory (~/quant_receipts for all three tools) with no 'verdict' key, violating the receipt-dir cross-lane contract that basis_executor.acquire() enforces (src/basis_executor.py:1015-1030: any verdict-less *.json in the receipt dir -> BLOCKED_UNRESOLVED) and that basis_position deliberately honors (STATE_VERDICT comment at src/basis_position.py:144-153; cmd_rates writes 'verdict': 'RATES_RECORDED'). One default-config watch pass permanently blocks every subsequent executor run.
findings.scenario: Run 'basis_watch --once' with default RECEIPT_DIR, then run the basis executor: acquire() lists basis_watch_state.json, finds no 'verdict' key, and every executor run exits BLOCKED_UNRESOLVED with the misleading instruction to 'reconcile its client ids' against a file that contains no orders, until an operator manually moves/deletes the watch state file (destroying watch persistence).

findings.claim: apply_decision sets state.state = 'PROPOSED' unconditionally even when try_focus denies focus capacity, so the advanced pool (FOCUS+PROPOSED, counted by _focus_pool) exceeds focus_hard_cap without bound — contradicting try_focus's documented invariant 'the hard cap is never exceeded' (the 'focus' kind correctly demotes to WATCHING on denial). Denied-but-PROPOSED symbols also never receive focus_since_ms, and maintain() only ages FOCUS states, so they have no capacity-driven or age-driven expiry.
findings.scenario: Verified by execution: with focus_soft_cap=1, focus_hard_cap=2, two weaker-scoring 'proposal' decisions both became PROPOSED, leaving 3 advanced symbols against a hard cap of 2. In a live loop, N proposal-grade symbols all hold advanced slots regardless of the cap; every one is re-added to the finalist list each pass (4 extra public GETs per symbol per pass), defeating the focus_capacity_hysteresis bound the state machine promises.

findings.claim: cmd_check performs an unlocked read-modify-write of the whole basis-position.json: it loads the position, spends seconds on public reads (gap_row with retries), then save_position() rewrites the entire file to record last_check. No lock coordinates position commands (the basis-executor.lock lane lock only blocks a new --open; --check/--close/--resume never acquire anything), so a concurrent --close or --resume — the designed usage is a --check hold loop plus owner-initiated --close — can have its just-persisted pending_intent/client_ids and state transition (OPEN->CLOSING) clobbered by check's stale full-file write, breaking the module's core contract that 'the exact order intent and client id are persisted BEFORE every mutation, so a crash between persist and POST leaves an id to query, never a mystery'.
findings.scenario: Hold loop starts a --check tick (loads position state OPEN, begins public reads). Owner runs --close: state->CLOSING saved, persist_intent saves pending_intent + client_ids for EXIT_SHORT, the reduce-only close is POSTed. The check tick's reads finish and save_position writes its stale copy: state reverts to OPEN, pending_intent and the EXIT_SHORT client id vanish from disk. If the close process then dies before its next save, --resume queries only the surviving client_ids and reports the pair OPEN while a submitted close order is invisible to query-first recovery — exactly the mystery the persist-before-mutation discipline exists to prevent.

CONFIRMED by code reading plus a live reproduction. basis_watch.py writes its state to RECEIPT_DIR/basis_watch_state.json by default (RECEIPT_DIR default ~/quant_receipts, line 108; default path joined at line 1252; run_pass unconditionally calls save_state at line 1193), and the save_state payload (lines 895-903) has only version/updated_utc/watermark/symbols — no 'verdict' key, and no occurrence of 'verdict' anywhere in the file. basis_executor.acquire (lines 1011-1030) scans every *.json in the same default receipt dir, skips only its own receipt filename, and finishes BLOCKED_UNRESOLVED on any dict without a 'verdict' key — no allowlist or state-file exemption exists. basis_position.py lines 143-153 + cmd_rates ('verdict': 'RATES_RECORDED', line 963) prove the cross-lane contract is deliberate and honored by the other lane. The behavioral oracle (old_engine_spec.json, scanner.state_machine.symbol_lifecycle) explicitly specifies {from: "any", on: "decision proposal", to: "PROPOSED", effect: "holds a focus slot when available"} — an unconditional transition to PROPOSED; the capacity-denied→WATCHING branch exists only for "decision focus". Line 986 is therefore a faithful port, and demoting denied proposals to WATCHING would violate the oracle. The "hard cap never exceeded" invariant governs granted focus slots (active_focus_count in the fixtures), and measured execution of the claimed scenario shows slot holders (focus_since_ms set) = 1 <= hard_cap 2 while try_focus never admits past the cap — denied-PROPOSED symbols hold no slot, exactly the spec's "slot when available". The claimed harms also fail: (a) _pick_finalists re-adds WATCHING symbols too, so the proposed demotion would cost the identical 4 GETs per symbol per pass — the cap never bounds finalist enrichment; (b) "no capacity-driven expiry" is false — denied-PROPOSED symbols are in _focus_pool and are evicted (capacity_evicted → WATCHING) when a stronger admission arrives at hard cap, verified by execution; (c) absence of an age TTL on PROPOSED matches the oracle, which expires proposals decision-driven (reject → COOLDOWN, watch → WATCHING+TTL, ignore → IDLE) on each pass's re-evaluation. All 601 offline tests pass. No money or order-flow impact: the observer places no orders.

CONFIRMED by execution. src/basis_watch.py:986 sets state="PROPOSED" unconditionally; try_focus's return gates only focus_since_ms. Measured with focus_soft_cap=1/hard_cap=2: one FOCUS(score 9) plus three weaker proposal decisions produced an advanced pool (FOCUS+PROPOSED, the code's own _focus_pool definition) of 4 against hard cap 2 — unbounded growth, violating try_focus's docstring "the hard cap is never exceeded" and the oracle's focus_capacity_hysteresis reason line. Also measured: maintain() at +100x focus_max_age_ms never removed the denied-PROPOSED symbols (age sweep fires only on state=="FOCUS" with focus_since_ms set; denied proposals have focus_since_ms=None), so they have no capacity- or age-driven expiry. Refutations failed: (1) the spec's "tryFocus best-effort, state=PROPOSED" is cap-safe in the original only via the pinned override ("pinned always enters, at hard cap evicts weakest unpinned") which the port omits entirely (no "pinned" in src) — so ordinary score denial, not the everything-pinned corner, now produces over-cap PROPOSED; (2) no reachability guard — persist_ticks accrues regardless of state (line 726), so capacity-denied WATCHING symbols reach proposal-kind; (3) no test covers proposal-under-denial (capacity tests use only "focus" kind); the full 601-test suite passes with the hole present. Consequences real: finalist builder (~line 1104) re-adds every PROPOSED symbol each pass with per-symbol enrichment fetches, so the state machine's capacity bound on per-pass work is defeated; ghost weak-score PROPOSED entries also distort future admissions (stronger focus can evict a PROPOSED symbol, weaker focus is denied against an inflated pool). Only the incidental "4 GETs per symbol" count was left unverified; the core defect is measured.

findings.claim: derive_resume declares CLOSED and cmd_resume releases the lane lock whenever any EXIT_SPOT/UNWIND_SPOT fill is nonzero, skipping the observed base-balance check entirely (`sold_spot or base_free < spot_step` short-circuits), so a partial spot exit with a proven sellable residual is reported as 'every leg terminal, futures flat, no sellable base' — violating the spec guard that CLOSED requires account-baseline-flat proof, unblocking new entries in both lanes while unhedged spot stands.
findings.scenario: Reproduced by direct call: position entered 1.0 spot + 1.0 short; --close fills EXIT_SHORT 1.0 and EXIT_SPOT terminal-partial 0.4 (cmd_close itself flags ONE_LEG_EXPOSED, printing '--resume reconciles'); owner runs --resume; queries return EXIT_SPOT executedQty 0.4 > 0, futures flat, base_free 0.6 with spot_step 0.001 (600x sellable). derive_resume returns state CLOSED / verdict CLOSED / note 'no sellable base' with zero recommendations; cmd_resume line 1785 then releases basis-executor.lock. 0.6 base of unhedged spot exposure stands untracked while --open and the one-shot executor are free to trade the same account.

findings.claim: cmd_close reads entry["short"]["filled_qty"] unconditionally, but a resume-proven OPEN position (short leg UNKNOWN during --open, then --resume proves the fill from the exchange — a path the test suite itself constructs) never had entry["short"] persisted, so the only exit command for OPEN crashes with an unhandled KeyError and the position cannot be closed through the CLI; the short quantity resume measured from positionRisk is discarded instead of persisted.
findings.scenario: Reproduced via the suite's own harness: --open with ENTER_SHORT submit unclear + query unclear -> state UNKNOWN; --resume with positionRisk -0.098 -> state OPEN, 'short' not in entry (test_resume_proves_unknown_short_filled pins this state); owner runs --close -> KeyError: 'short' traceback before any mutation. --check can meanwhile emit REQUEST_EXIT/MAXIMUM_HOLDING_HORIZON, but every close attempt dies; exit only possible by hand outside the machine.

findings.claim: After a partial reduce-only close (state CLOSING -> --resume derives OPEN), a second --close persists and submits the ORIGINAL entry short quantity from the stale entry snapshot rather than the remaining exchange position that resume itself just measured and stored in reconcile.futures_position, so live the reduce-only order exceeds the position and is rejected every attempt — the position becomes permanently unclosable through the CLI (the fake transport in tests masks this by filling the oversized quantity).
findings.scenario: Reproduced via the harness: OPEN with short 0.098; --close where EXIT_SHORT fills 0.05 of 0.098 -> OPEN_EXPOSURE/CLOSING; --resume with positionRisk -0.048 -> OPEN; second --close submits reduceOnly BUY quantity 0.098 against the 0.048 short. Binance rejects reduce-only orders exceeding the position (-2022), so cmd_close takes the 'rejected' branch, resets to OPEN, and every subsequent --close resubmits the same stale 0.098 forever; the hedged-but-shrunken pair can never be exited by the machine.

findings.claim: cmd_open enforces no verdict-less prior-receipt gate: both sibling lanes refuse to trade when any *.json in the shared receipt directory lacks a verdict (basis_executor.acquire lines 1015-1030 'whatever lane wrote it'; spot_roundtrip lines 328-338), and spot_roundtrip guards its exposure with its own run.lock which cmd_open never checks — so the position lane opens new exposure over a crashed sibling run's unreconciled client ids on the same account.
findings.scenario: spot_roundtrip (same default RECEIPT_DIR ~/quant_receipts) is killed mid-run: roundtrip-<rid>.json exists with no verdict and run.lock is on disk, its buy/sell orders possibly live. basis_executor --execute in that state refuses BLOCKED_UNRESOLVED; basis_position --open checks only basis-position.json state and basis-executor.lock, passes both, takes the lane lock, and submits a new spot BUY + futures SELL while the crashed run's ids are unreconciled — exactly the double-exposure case the sibling gates exist to block.

findings.claim: The resume latch sets thesis.opened_at_ms to local now_ms() instead of the exchange-reported fill time available in the just-queried order, so cmd_close's income window (startTime=opened_at) silently excludes the entry USDM COMMISSION row and every FUNDING_FEE accrued between the real fill and the resume while still printing total_usdt as a definite number, and the MAX_HOLD_MS risk clock starts late, holding the position beyond the owner's horizon.
findings.scenario: --open crashes/goes UNKNOWN after the short fills at T; owner runs --resume hours later at T+8h (one or more funding events elapsed); test_resume_proves_unknown_short_filled pins opened_at_ms = resume time. --close then queries /fapi/v1/income with startTime=T+8h: the entry commission (timestamped T) and the funding payments in (T, T+8h) are excluded, so pnl.total_usdt is computed and reported as exact while omitting real paid funding and commission — despite the code's own rule that funding is exchange truth never assumed.

findings.claim: _spot_usdt_fees sums only USDT-denominated commissions, so spot fees paid in BNB (a standard account setting; recorded in the persisted fee_by_asset exchange truth and reducing neither base quantity nor quote proceeds) are silently dropped from pnl.total_usdt with no UNKNOWN marker — the total is presented as exact while a real cost is missing.

result.reason: Confirmed by live reproduction with the suite's own harness. entry["short"] is written only in cmd_open on a terminal short fill (src/basis_position.py:1180); the short-unknown path persists the entry snapshot without it and exits UNKNOWN. cmd_resume/derive_resume promote to OPEN from positionRisk + terminal client-id proof but never write entry["short"] — the measured short goes only to reconcile.futures_position (line 1775), which cmd_close never reads. tests/test_basis_position.py:1228 (test_resume_proves_unknown_short_filled) pins exactly this OPEN-without-short state. cmd_close line 1451 reads entry["short"]["filled_qty"] unconditionally; reproduction yields KeyError('short') before any mutation or POST, state stays OPEN, and repeated resume/close cycles never repair it — the only CLI exit for a resume-proven OPEN position is permanently broken while --check can still demand REQUEST_EXIT. No guard, handler, or alternative quantity source exists (main() catches only PositionError from config).

Confirmed, not refuted. fees_by_asset (spot_roundtrip.py:211) persists ALL commission assets (including BNB) into fee_by_asset, but _spot_usdt_fees (basis_position.py:1419-1431) sums only asset == "USDT" (and silently swallows ArithmeticError). On the entry side (basis_position.py:1121-1137) quote_spent is the gross quote field and net_base subtracts only base-asset fees via base_fee_of (basis_executor.py:570-572, filters commissionAsset == base_asset), so a BNB commission on a non-BNB pair reduces neither base nor quote — exactly the claimed scenario. cmd_close's total_usdt (basis_position.py:1608-1613) goes UNKNOWN only for unreadable funding/USD-M income, never for foreign spot fee assets, so with BNB-paid spot fees spot_fees_usdt = 0 and the exact-looking total overstates realized P&L by the full BNB commission. No guard exists anywhere in src/ (no commissionAsset validation, no BNB-burn preflight, no foreign-asset UNKNOWN marker), and the only close-P&L test uses USDT-only fee fixtures. This is wrong money math with silent unsafety in a wave-3 file.

CONFIRMED. entry["short"]["filled_qty"] is written exactly once at open (basis_position.py:1180) and never updated. After a partial EXIT_SHORT fill, cmd_close persists CLOSING (lines 1485-1495, "--resume reconciles"); cmd_resume/derive_resume then derive ST_OPEN whenever short_amount != 0 and the spot leg filled (lines 1681-1692), storing the measured remaining short only in reconcile.futures_position (line 1775) without touching the entry snapshot. A second --close is admitted on state==OPEN (line 1441) and sizes the reduce-only BUY from the stale snapshot (line 1451, submitted at 1465); leg_intent (basis_cycle.py:155-157) and settle_leg (basis_executor.py:468) pass the quantity verbatim with no clamp to the live position. Live, Binance rejects a reduce-only order exceeding the position (-2022), settle_leg returns "rejected", closed<=0 resets state to OPEN ("hedged pair intact" — also factually wrong at that point), and every retry resubmits the same stale quantity: a permanent loop with no machine path that closes using the measured remainder. Even if a venue auto-clamped instead, closed<short_qty routes back to CLOSING, resume then derives ST_ONE_LEG (manual recommendation only, --close refuses), so the pair is still unclosable by the machine. No test covers partial-close→resume→close, and the fake transport fills any requested quantity, masking the live rejection. All refutation avenues (guards in cmd_close, snapshot refresh in resume, clamping in leg_intent/settle_leg, alternate derive_resume outcome) checked and absent.

CONFIRMED, dynamically. CONFIRMED by live reproduction with the suite's own harness. cmd_open persists position["entry"] (basis_position.py:1139-1154) before leg 2; the "short" key is only added at line 1180, unreachable when ENTER_SHORT resolves "unknown" (lines 1166-1173 return with state UNKNOWN). cmd_resume, on proving the short from positionRisk, sets state OPEN but records the measured quantity only as the string reconcile["futures_position"] (line 1775) — entry["short"] is never written; tests/test_basis_position.py:1228 (test_resume_proves_unknown_short_filled) pins exactly this persisted state ("Entry snapshot was never persisted"). cmd_close accepts only ST_OPEN (line 1441) and reads entry["short"]["filled_qty"] unconditionally at line 1451 with no guard anywhere (grep: no entry.get("short"), no "short" in entry, no KeyError handler; main() dispatch at 1831-1833 is bare).
